document.abstract: An historical review of theater television's growth from 1930 to 1949 is presented. The authors outline the status of theater television equipment used for direct or “film storage” projection, including an analysis of the radio-frequency requirements, methods of program distribution, and capital costs of a nation-wide theater television system. Some aspects of theater television programming are also presented.
